speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Sheaf cohomology and the preparation for Verdier duality
summary: Following the previous notebook\textquotesingle s discussion of sheaves, Beilinson develops sheafification, exactness, flabby resolutions, and cohomology. A finite-poset exercise connects the general formalism with combinatorial sheaves; the last page begins the compact-support dual construction needed for Verdier duality. These are foundational results, with hypotheses suppressed in several classroom formulations.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Dyson's constant term and Good's proof
summary: Gelfand presents the Dyson constant-term identity and the short interpolation proof attributed in the notebook to a name written as \ru{Вуда}. The exact recurrence and bibliographic year identify I. J. Good\textquotesingle s 1970 proof. The final induction ends at the top of P001390, before Veselov\textquotesingle s heading.

speaker: A. P. Veselov
title: Quadrics, the Neumann system, and two Poisson brackets
summary: Veselov compares geodesics on a quadric with the Neumann oscillator on a sphere using Kn\"orrer\textquotesingle s time change and Gauss map. He then presents a spectral-operator interpretation and two Hamiltonian descriptions in dimension three. Gelfand asks an inverse problem for a rank-one matrix perturbation; its uniqueness needs qualifications absent from the shorthand question.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Complexes, homotopy, and localization
summary: Beilinson moves from poset representations to complexes over an abelian category, homotopies, and quasi-isomorphisms. Roof diagrams and the Ore construction introduce the derived category. The same localization is revisited on 23 November; these occurrences are kept separate, with a cross-link rather than treated as new research.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Summation formulas and a parabolic double-coset algebra
summary: Gelfand derives a triangular system relating derivative sums to endpoint differences, leading to the Euler--Maclaurin formula. The same short contribution recalls the Coxeter presentation of a symmetric group and introduces the subalgebra invariant on both sides under a Young subgroup. The second topic ends at the top of P001396, before Beilinson resumes.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Truncation, mapping cones, and distinguished triangles
summary: Beilinson continues the derived-category course after Gelfand\textquotesingle s intervention. He explains how cohomology in one degree identifies a complex in the derived category, contrasts this with splitting in several degrees, and introduces mapping cones and exact triangles. Several signs and the ordering of cone summands require explicit conventions.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Symmetric functions and Schubert polynomials after Lascoux
summary: Gelfand develops symmetric functions in alphabet notation, determinant identities, and Schubert polynomials via divided differences. The finite coinvariant ring, its pairing, and the symmetric-group action connect these formulas with flag cohomology. The final request for a character interpretation had already been answered in the appropriate Borel-module category by the 1986 preprint and 1987 announcement of Kra\'skiewicz and Pragacz; the notebook\textquotesingle s word irreducible needs qualification.

speaker: M. M. Kapranov
title: Double categories, two-categories, and higher fundamental groupoids
summary: Kapranov introduces squares with horizontal and vertical composition, the structure now conventionally called a double category, and its interchange axiom. Kontsevich contrasts this with two-morphisms between parallel arrows. A tensor-contraction example, Gelfand\textquotesingle s boundary-value suggestion, and the homotopy squares of a filtered space give three distinct motivations.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Derived categories: the cone lemma and roofs, revisited
summary: This one-page continuation recalls the categories of complexes, homotopy classes, and derived morphisms. It states the cone proof of the Ore lemma and the equivalence relation on roofs. The outgoing quasi-isomorphism is written on the wrong leg of the opening diagram, an error visible in the original scan.

speaker: I. S. Zakharevich
title: Bernoulli coding, the baker map, and hyperbolicity
summary: The short talk illustrates sensitivity to finite observational precision using the two-sided binary shift and the baker transformation. A closing comparison invokes geodesic flow on a negatively curved manifold. Measure-theoretic coding, topological conjugacy, and deterministic loss of exact information must be distinguished.

speaker: G. A. Margulis
title: Rational iteration, Sullivan's theorem, and fractal questions
summary: Margulis moves from affine maps and squaring to the Fatou and Julia sets of a rational map, then sketches Sullivan\textquotesingle s quasiconformal proof excluding wandering domains. Gelfand\textquotesingle s interventions include circle linearization, elementary measure and dimension exercises, and a programme for discrete-group representations on fractal sets. The final disk-packing sketch omits the iterative rule needed for either residual-set question.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Matroids, bimatroids, and determinant relations
summary: Gelfand revisits representability through the Fano configuration, basis exchange, and the nonzero minors of a matrix. Several questions are already classical, while the comparison with an uncertain named author and the request to discretize an entire syzygy chain lack a determinate target. The literal determinant identity contains several errors; a corrected exchange identity explains the intended argument.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Kerov’s Hecke representations and Frobenius characters
summary: Gelfand explicitly expounds Kerov\textquotesingle s work: Hecke generators, Young-tableau adjacency, and rational weights give an orthogonal-form construction. The seminar then asks for Hecke characters and recalls the ordinary Frobenius formula. The latter ends above the divider on P001416; the following Ruelle-zeta discussion belongs to record 727.
